item.title: Kitten Crying Alone Inside NY Construction Site Started Purring the Second He Was Lifted Into Someone's Arms
item.description:
A gray tabby kitten was crying alone somewhere inside a construction site when a kind woman finally coaxed him out, and the instant she lifted him into her arms, the tiny kitten started to purr, as though he had been waiting his whole short life to be found.

AshCredit: For Animals Inc.

Ash's rescue was the happy accident at the center of a much greater effort that had been underway for months. Back in April, a woman living in a Queens housing project reached out to For Animals Inc. for help with the cats in her neighborhood.

A devoted volunteer named Jenn had been lending a hand ever since, caring for the colony this woman feeds and for another feeder's cats in the same project. It was patient, steady work that had been going on long before Ash was anywhere in the picture.

Before construction began in the area in late May, the team had already trapped and neutered several of the cats as part of the slow, steady trap-neuter-return practice that keeps a colony healthy and from growing.

The construction site where Ash was found crying, all aloneCredit: For Animals Inc.

In mid-September, Jenn went back to trap four more cats. Months of construction work had been done at that time, and it was that very return that put someone close enough to hear him. The day after they trapped those four successfully, the feeder caught the unmistakable sound of a kitten crying.

Somewhere in the fenced-off construction area, a little one was alone and calling out. With gentle patience, the feeder managed to lure the frightened baby into the open with some food, and the moment she picked him up, he melted every heart within reach.

The purr that started it allCredit: For Animals Inc.

This tiny kitten, only about nine weeks old, began to purr the second he was in her hands. "As soon as the woman who found him picked him up, he was purring in her arms," For Animals Inc. shared with LoveMeow.

She contacted Jenn right away, who came to collect the little one and has been lovingly fostering him ever since. From that first purr in a stranger's arms, it was clear Ash had an abundance of love to give, and that he had landed with exactly the right people to help him flourish.

A rough start, firmly behind him nowCredit: For Animals Inc.

When Ash first came into care, he was not in great shape. The poor baby was dehydrated and had worms and diarrhea, the rough start so many kittens born outdoors endure.

In the steady care of his foster, he was dewormed, nursed back to health, and given everything a growing kitten needs. Today he is completely healthy and thriving, with all of those early troubles behind him.

All personality, once he felt safeCredit: For Animals Inc.

And what a personality he turned out to have. "Ash is super playful, sweet, and cuddly," For Animals Inc. shared with our team. "He loves nap times with his humans and playtime with the kitties."

He is equally content to flop into a lap or launch into a chase, the sort of kitten who brings a room to life the moment he tumbles into it.

Easygoing enough to share a home with a dogCredit: For Animals Inc.

He is also proving to be a wonderfully adaptable little guy. "He is in a foster home with a large dog, and while not a huge fan yet, he is totally fine with her," the rescue shared.

For a kitten who spent his first weeks fending for himself outdoors, that easy confidence around a dog many times his size says a great deal about his gentle, trusting nature.

A serious look from a decidedly unserious kittenCredit: For Animals Inc.

Ash has tested negative for both FIV and FeLV, and he will be neutered once he is a little older. Beyond those few practicalities, he is a completely healthy, happy boy.

Every bit of his bright beginning traces back to the people who refused to leave him crying in that construction site. From the feeder who lured him to safety, to Jenn who has fostered and nurtured him, to the whole For Animals Inc. team caring for this community's cats, Ash has been surrounded by kindness from the start.

Play first, questions laterCredit: For Animals Inc.

That kindness is written all over the kitten he has become. The baby who was calling out from behind a construction fence now has warm laps to nap on, friends to chase, and nothing left to cry about.

He carries none of the fear of those first days. After everything he faced out there, Ash met the people who came for him with a purr, and he has kept purring ever since.

Ash, ready for whatever comes nextCredit: For Animals Inc.

Not long ago, Ash was a nine-week-old kitten alone on a construction site, crying for someone to come. Today he is healthy, playful, and thoroughly adored, a purring charmer who took to being loved as though he had always expected it.

The kitten who started purring the second he was picked up has not really stopped, and whoever finds him next will hear it from the very first moment.

item.title: Mama Cat and Her Five Kittens Gravely Ill Behind a Nail Salon Refused to Give Up, and Pulled Through Together
item.description:
A mother cat and her five kittens were found behind a nail salon so sick that the babies might not have lived another week, and today, against those odds, the whole little family is healing and growing stronger by the day.

The Nail Salon KittensCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

Their story began behind a nail salon in the Bronx, where a mama cat and her five kittens were discovered tucked out of sight. Someone named them for where they were found, and the theme stuck: Mani, Pedi, Tips, Baby Buff, and Polly Polish, with their devoted mother, Frenchie.

The find was not a happy one at first. The kittens were critically ill, some with symptoms as frightening as severe diarrhea, and without rescue and intensive care, these fragile babies would not have survived.

The caring team at The Cat Collective Rescue NY pulled them into safety just in time, and the real work began, because a weak mother and five failing kittens needed far more than a warm place to land.

The spot behind the salon where the family was surviving Credit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

The spot behind the salon is hard to look at, knowing a weak mother and five sick kittens had been surviving there with nowhere else to go. Frenchie had been holding the whole family together on nothing at all.

It showed the moment she was found. She was running on empty, and her babies were slipping, which made getting all six of them into safety a race against the clock.

Frenchie, who gave everything she had to keep her babies aliveCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

From the first day in rescue, the family got truly around-the-clock care. There were medications to give and high-calorie supplements to build the babies up, along with special food, constant cleaning, and litter boxes changed several times a day.

Every one of them was watched over closely, and above all, they were showered with love. For a family that had been getting by on scraps and luck, it was the first steady care any of them had known.

Polly Polish, the smallest, beforeCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

All five kittens were very sick, but little Polly Polish was the most fragile of them, hovering near death and needing more help than the others. That is when Nicola Jones, a volunteer who takes on the most fragile cases, stepped forward and agreed to nurse the tiny girl back to health.

Under her gentle, dedicated care, Polly got the fighting chance she so badly needed. The smallest of the Nail Kittens turned out to have one of the biggest wills to live.

Polly Polish NowCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

Through it all, no one worked harder for these babies than their mama. When Frenchie was found, she was little more than skin and bones, having given every ounce of her own strength to nurse five kittens while she herself went hungry.

Her gentle spirit touched everyone who met her. "She is one of the sweetest cats I have ever met," The Cat Collective Rescue NYC shared with LoveMeow. "She takes her medicine without a fight. She rubs against your legs. She looks up at you and gives the softest, most heartbreaking little meow."

Baby Buff after a washCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

Caring for a sick mother and five sick kittens at once was no small undertaking, and it came during an already difficult stretch for the rescue. Cat Collective NY refused to give up on this family anyway, pouring in time, energy, and heart even when resources were thin.

They did not do it alone. Alongside Nicola nursing Polly and the foster providing constant daily care, a whole community gathered around the Nail Kittens, and the tide began to turn for all six of them.

Baby Buff nowCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

The results of all that devotion have been wonderful to watch. The Nail Kittens are healing beautifully, each of them gaining weight, eating on their own, and growing stronger with each passing day.

The sickly little ones who once needed round-the-clock intervention are now fully kittens, busy, hungry, and getting into everything, exactly as they should be. Tips leads the mischief, Mani and Pedi tumble after him, and Baby Buff keeps pace like he was never the smallest thing on a vet table.

TipsCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

As The Cat Collective Rescue NY put it, they may have taken this family off the street, but it was the community who truly rescued them. From the volunteer who nursed the sickest kitten back to health, to the foster providing constant care, to everyone who shared the family's story, Frenchie and her babies have been carried by an outpouring of kindness.

Polly Polish, once hovering near death, is proof of how far that kindness reached. The kitten no one was sure would make it is now keeping right up with her littermates.

PediCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

The kittens continue to flourish, growing into the playful, healthy little cats they were always meant to be. Where there was once a row of fragile patients, there is now a pile of ordinary chaos.

Each of them carries a piece of their origin story in their name, from Mani and Pedi to Tips, Baby Buff, and Polly Polish, a cheeky set of souvenirs from the salon that nobody who meets them will soon forget.

ManiCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

Their mama, meanwhile, is still looking for a place of her own. After giving so much of herself for her babies, Frenchie is searching for a foster or a forever home, somewhere she can be the one who is cared for.

She has earned it many times over. The cat who arrived as skin and bones, still purring and still gentle, gave everything she had before anyone thought to give anything back to her.

Frenchie, ready for her next adventureCredit: The Cat Collective Rescue NY

After everything this brave family endured behind a nail salon, their story has turned into one of healing. The five kittens who nearly did not make it are thriving, and the mother who went hungry to keep them alive is finally being looked after herself.

Frenchie and her five babies have come a very long way from that hidden spot in the Bronx. For the first time in their lives, every one of them is safe, fed, and surrounded by people who refused to look away.

Share this story with your friends. View more on Frenchie, the Nail Kittens, and The Cat Collective Rescue NY on @catcollectiveny. Follow Nicola Jones, the volunteer who nursed Polly Polish back to health, on Instagram @harlemkittiechick1.

Related Story: Family Adopted Kittens Then Came Back for Their Mother Cat, Leading to the Sweetest Reunion

item.title: Kitten Born With an Enlarged Heart Was Called "Defective" and Took the Biggest Week of His Life in Stride
item.description:
A white kitten was dropped at a pound labeled "defective" and marked high-risk due to an enlarged heart. The kitten who came out the other side has turned into perhaps the most loving little cat his rescuers have ever met.

Big HeartCredit: Heather T

Big Heart lives up to his name in every sense, figuratively and quite literally. He was born with a congenital heart condition, and one part of it means his heart is actually enlarged, which is where his name comes from.

That condition is also what nearly ended his story before it began. He was surrendered to a pound with the claim that he was defective and should be put down, a death sentence handed to a kitten who had done nothing but be born a little different.

His story was never going to end there, though, because the right person saw him in time.

Safe at last, the day his real life beganCredit: Heather T

The director of Love Your Feral Felines spotted Big Heart and refused to let him go. She fought for him, secured the approval needed to pull him out, and got the tiny patient the second chance no one at the pound had been willing to give.

That was only the first hurdle. The next was getting him safely neutered, with everyone hoping his delicate heart would handle it. He came through the procedure like a champion, then rode out the hour-long drive to his foster home like a seasoned traveler, taking the biggest week of his short life completely in stride.

Gentle, but play time around the cornerCredit: Heather T

Settled into foster care, Big Heart has been, by every account, a dream. His foster, Heather T. of The 2 Pound Kitten Club, keeps his play gentle and his world calm to protect his heart, and the remarkable thing is that he seems to understand his own limits.

Hop Hop! Credit: Heather T

Give him a string to chase and his careful, happy nature shows itself. "He is self-regulating so he doesn't overdo it to make his heart work too hard," Heather shared with LoveMeow, and sure enough, he plays with real delight and then eases off on his own, never pushing past what his heart can handle. In every other way, he is a normal, happy kitten having a completely normal, happy time.

I know I'm cuteCredit: Heather T

item.title: Odd-Eyed Kitten Found Pregnant in the Bronx Had Every Reason to Give Up, Now Basks in the Sun Each Day
item.description:
A six-month-old kitten with one blue eye and one green eye was found pregnant in the streets of the Bronx, NY. She had every reason to give up. Now she basks in the sun of each new day.

IrisCredit: Astoria Paws Cats

The first thing anyone notices about Iris is her eyes. One is a clear sky blue, the other a bright green, set in a soft white and tabby colored face that turns toward every bit of sunlight it can find. The trait is heterochromia, a harmless genetic condition where a cat has two different-colored eyes.

The second thing is how sweet she is, which is remarkable given how little reason she was given. At just six months old, Iris has already been through more than most cats face in a lifetime.

She was found on the streets of the Bronx, pregnant and alone, far too young to be carrying a litter. By the time she was rescued, her kittens had not survived.

Safe in a carrierCredit: Astoria Paws Cats

Her luck turned when a young woman who looks out for the cats in her Bronx neighborhood spotted her and stepped in. She got Iris off the street and into safety, the first kind hand this kitten had known.

From there, Astoria Paws Cats made sure she got everything she had gone without. She was spayed, looked over, and allowed, maybe for the first time, to rest somewhere warm. "She remains the sweetest, gentlest, most affectionate little soul," Vanessa A. of the rescue shared with LoveMeow, a cat who met everything that happened to her and stayed soft anyway.

A full bowl and a feeder of her own, no more scavenging requiredCredit: Astoria Paws Cats

There is a small ear tip on one of her ears, the notch clinics use to mark a cat who has been fixed and returned to the outdoors. Iris got hers by accident. She was never meant to go back out. She was always meant to be somebody's.

Vanessa does not hide how much that one mistake stung. "She was never supposed to return to the streets," she shared. The notch changes nothing about the cat underneath it, a young, affectionate girl who was always headed for a home.

Iris discovers the lick-treatCredit: Astoria Paws Cats

Watch Iris at snack time and the hard start falls away entirely. She leans in for a lick treat, eyes half closed, tongue going, the picture of a cat who has figured out that good things happen here now.

It is a small moment, but it says a lot about how far she has come. The kitten who once scavenged to stay alive now waits by her own feeder and takes her snacks from a trusting hand.

Looking up for attentionCredit: Astoria Paws Cats

Food is not the only thing she lights up for. Iris adores attention, and she is not shy about asking, reaching up a white paw and fixing those two different eyes on you until you give in.

She turned out to be the easiest kind of cat to fall for, affectionate and trusting despite every reason not to be. She wants to be near her people, folded up close, soaking in the kind of steady love she spent her first months without.

Time well spent Credit: Astoria Paws Cats

She has a playful side, too, and it comes out more every day. Given a toy to chase, Iris pounces and bats and tumbles after it with the bright, uncomplicated joy of a kitten who finally feels safe enough to let loose.

She plays the way only a truly relaxed cat does, all in, a little silly, worn out and happy by the end. It is the clearest sign yet that she has completely left the street behind.

A sunny windowsill suits her perfectlyCredit: Astoria Paws Cats

When the games wind down, her favorite job is sunbathing. Iris claims the warmest windowsill in the house and settles in, her white coat glowing and her mismatched eyes catching the light, as she watches the world go by from the safe side of the glass.

She has grown comfortable enough to be curious, too, peering down at the room below and tracking every small event with the mild interest of a cat who no longer has anything to fear.

A long, warm stretch in her favorite patch of lightCredit: Astoria Paws Cats

In her quietest moments, she basks, rolling into the sun and stretching out without a care, the kind of deep, easy rest that only comes when a cat feels truly safe.

For a kitten who began life with nothing soft to lie on, a warm square of floor and all the time in the world to enjoy it is close to everything.

Pouncing skills on display Credit: Astoria Paws Cats

Iris is six months old, and the hardest chapter of her short life is already behind her. The gentle, striking, deeply affectionate young cat who came through it has been adopted and is now settled in her forever home

She has one blue eye, one green eye, a small notch in her ear, and a person who looked at it all and saw only a beautiful cat. After she was found, and thanks to the neighbor who first got her off the street, Iris got the ending she always deserved.

item.title: September's Five Most Read Rescues, Starting With a Mama Cat Who Hid Seven Kittens Under a Fallen Tree
item.description:
Every month, LoveMeow's editorial team reports original cat rescue stories sourced directly from shelters, foster families, and rescue organizations in the United States and beyond. These are the five stories that drew the most readers in September 2026, ranked by total page views.

The 5 Best Cat Rescue Stories of September 2026

Millie and her babiesCredit: Lori White

1. A Mama Cat Hid Seven Kittens Under a Fallen Tree Outside a Senior Living Facility and Kept Every One of Them Alive

Mildred, called Millie, had been surviving outdoors for months when someone noticed movement under a fallen tree on the grounds of a senior living facility on the south side of Indianapolis, Indiana. Underneath were seven kittens, roughly two and a half to three weeks old, five boys and two girls.

Alliance for Responsible Pet Ownership took the call, and the response was immediate. "We couldn't say no to helping them, so we quickly made some calls, and within 15 minutes my husband and daughter arrived with old towels, Churu, and carriers," foster Lori White said. The whole family came in together.

The kittens were named for the place that sheltered them: Norman, Stanley, Bernard, Eugene, and Otis Henry, with Dottie and Pearl Louise. Somebody christened the litter the Golden Years Gang, and the name stuck. Millie is regaining the weight she lost raising seven kittens on whatever she could find, and all eight of them are indoors now.

Read the Golden Years Gang's full story

Truly Scrumptious Credit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

2. A Cat Was Passed From Home to Home for Years Until a Single Microchip Scan Sent Him Back to the People Who Raised Him

Truly Scrumptious was adopted as a kitten in 2022 from Whiskers-A-GoGo, a volunteer-run rescue in Brooklyn, New York. Then his adopter's relationship ended, and the gray cat began moving. One home, then another, then a caretaker whose landlord would not allow him. He ended up on a Brooklyn sidewalk.

A rescuer named Bronwen found him there and did the one thing that changed everything: she scanned him. The chip led straight back to Whiskers-A-GoGo, which had never stopped being listed as his people. They brought him home.

It took about three weeks for him to understand that the moving had stopped. What emerged was a cat who holds hands while he is being cuddled and plays fetch with toy mice. Nobody had been looking for him. His microchip was the only thing that remembered he belonged somewhere.

Read Truly's full story

Jagger and JewellCredit: Best Friends Felines

3. Two Tonkinese Cats Pulled Off the Street Are Too Shy to Approach Anyone Alone and Entirely Different When They Have Each Other

Jagger and Jewell came off the streets of south-east Queensland, Australia, and into foster care with Best Friends Felines. Both have the pale blue eyes of their breed. Apart, they are two frightened cats. Together, they are something else.

"They take comfort from one another and rely on each other for confidence as they navigate the world around them," Judy of Best Friends Felines said. The rescue is honest about where each of them is. Of Jewell: "In time she may become a lap cat, but this will take a significant amount of time and patience." Of Jagger: "He is not at the stage where he will allow pats but is very curious about the goings-on in his current foster home."

He did let a veterinarian lift him out of his carrier and weigh him without a struggle, which for a cat at his stage is a considerable thing. They are available for adoption, and they are going together.

Read Jagger and Jewell's full story

'Squash' babiesCredit: Sonora Cat Rescue

4. Five Feral Kittens Could Not Be Touched Without Thick Gloves and Changed Their Minds in Under Two Days

Sonora Cat Rescue, an all-volunteer group in Sonora, California, had been trapping at the same residential property for two years, where elderly homeowners feed a feral colony. In September, the group brought in five kittens, roughly six weeks old: Acorn, Spaghetti, ButterNut, Patty Pan, and Zucchini.

They arrived unhandleable. They did not stay that way. "It hasn't even been 2 full days, and these spice nuggets I couldn't grab without gloves are now approaching me, leaning into scritches, and even purring," said Sadie Anderson, the rescue's president.

Anderson explained why the timing mattered so much. "When kittens are 5 to 8 weeks old, their personalities are very malleable," she said. "Once they get to be around 9 weeks old, that window slams shut." Five kittens came out of a colony inside that window, and five kittens are now fully socialized. They are preparing to join another rescued group known as the Cheers gang.

Read the squash kittens' full story

Dove TreeCredit: The Stray Cat Club

5. A Kitten Found Alone in a Cardboard Box Weighed 288 Grams and Now Pushes Around an 88-Pound Dog

Dove Tree was found on a public green in South East London, alone in a cardboard box, with no mother and no siblings anywhere nearby. The Stray Cat Club took her in.

She was so small that everyone assumed she was two or three weeks old. She was closer to five, and severely malnourished, weighing 288 grams. That gap between her size and her age is the whole measure of how long she had been without food.

She eats regularly now and gains steadily, and the personality that arrived with the weight has gone in an unexpected direction. "We're also beginning to see her funny little personality shining through more and more each day, including bullying the resident 40kg dog," the rescue reported. The dog in question is a gentle giant of roughly 88 pounds who appears to have accepted the arrangement.

Read Dove Tree's full story

item.title: Cat With a Neck Wound No One Could Heal Now Chooses to Strut Around in a Turtleneck
item.description:
A black-and-white tuxedo cat had an open wound no one could heal. Now, he chooses to strut around the home in a turtleneck.

Sir PurrCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Sir Purr is a lot of cat. He is a big, four-year-old tuxedo who carries himself like a kitten a fraction of his size, and who has apparently never been told that he is not, in fact, pocket-sized.

His road to that foster-home strut started at a New York City municipal shelter, where a rescue called Whiskers-A-GoGo pulled him from the crowd. He arrived with what everyone understood to be a healing wound, and at first he seemed well on his way.

After a few weeks, it became clear the wound was not healing at all. Sir Purr isn't quite ready for a home yet, and the reason turned out to be a small mystery that took a whole team to solve.

Sir Purr, announcing himself the day he came into rescueCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

One of the first things his rescuers learned is that Sir Purr has opinions and shares them freely. He announced himself from his carrier with a wide-mouthed meow, the kind of greeting that makes clear this is a cat who intends to be part of the conversation.

The wound itself sat in a spot that made it hard to protect. He didn't qualify for a cone or a bandage, and any bandage anyone tried, he removed within minutes. So he scratched, and the scratching sent him back to the vet again, and again, and again.

The wound that refused to heal, and kept sending him back to the vetCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

For a while the wound refused to explain itself. A veterinary clinic in Bushwick, the Neighborhood Vet, took him in to board and get to the bottom of it, and the answer didn't come quickly. It took repeated visits, a run of diagnostics, and more than one consultation with skin specialists before the picture finally became clear.

Through all the handling and rechecks, Sir Purr stayed the picture of patience, content to rest in someone's hands while they worked. The answer, when it came, was manageable. He is dealing with some skin irritation and allergies, and with the right treatment, things finally started looking up.

Turtleneck on, chin up, ready for a very important announcementCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

His real breakthrough arrived in his foster home, in the form of a tiny turtleneck. Snug over his shoulders, it keeps his busy claws off his healing skin, and it has turned a medical necessity into the most distinguished look in the house.

He wears it, frankly, beautifully. Perched on a step ladder in his teal turtleneck with his whiskers fanned out, Sir Purr looks less like a patient and more like a cat about to give a very important speech. Whiskers-A-GoGo's Eva put the verdict plainly: he looks "absolutely fire in his little turtleneck."

When the sun goes down, the zoomies beginCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

It took about a week for Sir Purr to show his foster family exactly who he is. "He is sweet, cuddly, and very much a people cat," Eva of Whiskers-A-GoGo shared with LoveMeow, a cat who soaks up every scrap of attention that comes his way. Toss him one of the small mice toys he loves and he will chase it clear across the room.

And then the sun goes down. "Once the sun goes down, he loves to have the zoomies all over," Eva shared with us, and the cuddly gentleman becomes a blur of black and white tearing joyful laps around the room.

For a cat who hates being alone, even a stuffed panda helpsCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

For all his swagger, Sir Purr is a gentle giant, and his foster says his favorite place in the world is stretched out on your chest while you lie down, purring like a small child who has gotten exactly what he wanted. He flops belly up without a care, a substantial cat who would like to be treated like a lap kitten, and his caregivers are only too happy to oblige.

His foster has also noticed something that matters for whoever takes him home. Sir Purr gets lonely, and a bored Sir Purr grows restless, so he is not a cat who will be content left to his own devices for long. Even a stuffed panda is better company than an empty room.

Two cats, no complaintsCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Company suits him, and he went looking for it. A four-month-old kitten is fostering in the same home, and Sir Purr couldn't resist him, curling up close and folding the two of them into a single small hut without a hint of protest. For all his size, he plays gently with the little one, and a feline companion would likely be a welcome addition wherever he lands.

He may not stop at cats, either. His foster watched him hang around the dogs at the vet without a trace of worry, which suggests this friendly giant is happy to count just about anyone as a friend. Eva sums up his whole outlook as "the more friends, the better."

Reaching across the floor for his buddy, because why nap aloneCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

The two of them have become a matched set, stretched across the floor with their paws reaching toward each other even at rest. Sir Purr is, in his foster's affectionate words, "a boss," a cat who knows exactly what he wants. He communicates his preferences and will let his person know, in his own direct way, when he is hungry, when he wants to play, and when he has had enough.

When Sir Purr finally does settle, he settles all the way. He sprawls across the best chair in the house. He falls deeply, thoroughly asleep, and his foster reports that he is a committed and enthusiastic snorer, which somehow only makes the giant baby more endearing.

The distinguished gentleman, off dutyCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

Whatever he wears, Sir Purr commits to it. In a tropical-print shirt, he looks ready for a vacation he has earned, and carries the whole production off without a shred of self-consciousness.

Between costume changes, the distinguished gentleman goes off duty. He rests on the nearest surface, and lets the day drift by like a cat with absolutely nowhere to be.

Feeling the tropic vibeCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

A wound that wouldn't heal brought a whole team together to figure Sir Purr out, and what they found underneath it was a four-year-old cat who is convinced he is a kitten, dressed like a gentleman, and certain that everyone is a friend not made yet.

He is longer and lankier than he thinks, and entirely at home stretched across a foster-home floor. When the day comes that he is fully healed, the family that finds him will get a substantial, turtleneck-clad, softly snoring companion who wants nothing more than to be part of everything.

No alarm set hereCredit: Whiskers-A-GoGo

item.title: Kitten Carried Into a Rescue in a Crumpled Paper Bag Was Never Going to Let It Be the End of His Story
item.description:
A tabby kitten was carried into a rescue tucked inside a paper bag that had been crumpled almost shut, and from the moment someone looked inside and saw his face, that bag was never going to be where his story ended.

CharlieCredit: Heather T

The day Charlie arrived, the rescue was not supposed to be taking anyone new. Love Your Feral Felines, the rescue known as LYFF, was on an intake freeze, with so many cats already in its care that the team made the hard, responsible call to pause new arrivals. They knew they could only stretch their people and resources so far and still do right by every cat already counting on them.

Then a person turned up carrying a tiny kitten in a paper bag, the top crumpled nearly shut. They could no longer keep him and had nowhere else to turn. For a kitten that small, with nowhere left to go, the clock was already running down.

The team could have said no. Instead, intake freeze and all, they said yes. "We weren't planning for another intake today, but rescue doesn't always stick to the plan," LYFF wrote afterward, and they took Charlie in that same day.

The bag Charlie arrived in, crumpled nearly shutCredit: Love Your Feral Felines

Set on a ledge, the bag is hard to look at even empty. Its handles are still twisted upright, its sides collapsed inward, and it is difficult to picture a living kitten folded inside with nowhere else to go.

That bag came very close to being the end for a kitten so small. "He would have died," Heather T., of LYFF, shared with LoveMeow.

The face that stopped the rescuers in their tracks, peering up from the paper bagCredit: Love Your Feral Felines

The first photos show the face that changed their minds. A small tabby with enormous green eyes peers up from a nest of brown paper, ears back, whiskers wide. He did not cry or thrash. He only looked up and waited to see what would happen next.

LYFF put it plainly when they shared his story. "We looked inside that bag, saw that little face, and knew we couldn't walk away," they wrote. "So we stepped in." Saying yes meant stretching an already full house even further, and they did not hesitate.

These days, every reaching hand means a chin scratchCredit: Heather T

From that point on, Charlie was no longer a kitten in a paper bag with nowhere to go. He was safe with LYFF, and everything he had been missing began arriving at once: good food, a warm bed, vaccines, a vet's attention, a neuter down the road, and far more hands than he knew what to do with.

He took to the affection right away. Rolled onto his back for a chin scratch with his eyes half closed; Charlie leans into every hand that reaches for him, as though he has decided that people are wonderful after all.

Room, at last, to stretch out and just be a kittenCredit: Heather T

For the first time in his short life, he has room to be a kitten and nothing else. No more crumpled paper, no more wondering where he will end up, only a soft blanket and a long afternoon to stretch across it.

His confidence has grown by the day. The nervous face from the bag has given way to a curious, bright-eyed tabby who inspects every corner of the room and greets each new person like a friend he has not met yet.

Charlie has decided climbing is the best thing in the worldCredit: Heather T

Climbing, he has discovered, is the best thing in the world. Charlie scrambles up his scratching post, peeks around it at whoever is watching, and hurls himself into play with the full engine of a healthy kitten.

Taking him in meant one more kitten to feed in a house that was already stretched thin, and the team never treated it as a burden. They found the room, shifted what they had to, and let the freeze bend for exactly one small tabby.

Safe in a cozy hut of his ownCredit: Heather T

A paper bag, crumpled almost shut, was never going to be the end of Charlie. Today he is tucked into a cozy hut of his own, a bright-eyed tabby peeking out at a world that turned out to be far kinder than his first day suggested.

Share this story with your friends. View more on Charlie and Heather T on Instagram @the2poundkittenclub. Love Your Feral Felines can be found on Facebook and Instagram @loveyourferalfelines.

item.title: Kitten Found Alone Outside at a Month Old Can Go From Lap-Melting Cuddles to Full Chaos in a Minute
item.description:
A long-haired grey kitten was found all alone outside when he was barely a month old, and a year later, he has grown into a cat who can go from lap-melting cuddles to full-speed chaos in the space of a single minute.

GreysonCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

This week, Greyson had a birthday. He turned one year old on September 22, a milestone that once looked a long way off.

He arrived at Pet Haven Minnesota last October as a tiny orphan, found outside on his own with no mother or littermates nearby. He was small enough to need round-the-clock bottle feeding, and a foster volunteer named Kris stepped in to give him exactly what was required.

That was nearly a year ago. Greyson has spent every day since in foster care, now with a foster named Jada, and he is still looking for the family who gets to keep him.

Greyson as the palm-sized bottle baby LoveMeow first metCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

When LoveMeow first shared his story, Greyson was a palm-sized bundle of gray fluff with a very big voice. He cried loudly for his meals and made his opinions known long before he could walk in a straight line.

Feeding him was not straightforward. He could only take small amounts at a time and did better sitting upright, so Kris fed him often and carefully, one small meal after another, until the weight began to come.

Barely bigger than the hand that fed him, and already all fluffCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

He was a fighter from the beginning. Greyson met every hurdle in front of him and kept growing fluffier and stronger, purring through all of it as though the hard parts belonged to someone else.

Early on, his fosters learned he had been born with a condition called congenital megacolon. A veterinary technician foster named Abby led the effort to manage it, and after a series of medication and diet trials, they found the routine that keeps him well.

Growing up in foster care, one scratcher box at a timeCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

Today that routine is a small, easy part of his day, and the rescue is proud of how well he does with it. "He takes everything like a champ; it's very easy, and his personality outweighs any medical needs," Eleanor, the marketing coordinator at Pet Haven Minnesota, told LoveMeow.

His condition, in other words, is close to the least interesting thing about him. Kris, the volunteer who bottle-raised him, sums Greyson up as "an energetic mix of playful yet cuddly," and that blend is the first thing most people notice.

Greyson at the wheel of his cardboard getaway truckCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

Eleanor puts it another way, describing him as "a little Jekyll and Hyde, which is amazing." One version of Greyson is pure motion, a gray streak who dives through tunnels and treats a cardboard truck like a getaway car.

He carries the full engine of a one-year-old cat and sees no reason to hide it. Toys go flying, tunnels get conquered, and anyone willing to join the game becomes his favorite person for the afternoon.

The tornado winding down, whiskers and allCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

Then, with very little warning, the other Greyson arrives. The switch tends to flip first thing in the morning, or the moment he spots someone he loves.

The cat who was a gray streak a minute ago melts into the nearest lap. "He runs to you. He's purring. He wants a million headbutts, a million pets," Eleanor said.

Settled into a favorite spotCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

That purr is his signature. Kris credits Greyson with "an excellent (and loud) purr motor that runs non-stop," and he leans into every scratch like he has been saving it up all day.

In Jada's home now, he is in no hurry about any of it. "If he can sit on your lap, he will just roll around for 10 minutes straight," Eleanor said. Greyson does not do much halfway, and affection is no exception.

A full year older, surveying the room he has grown up inCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

For all that charm, a full year has gone by, and Greyson is still in foster care. Greyson has grown up, filled out, learned the house, and met every visitor with the same open heart, but the right person hasn't walked in yet.

Pet Haven continues to advocate for the greatest care for him. Greyson, for his part, looks entirely ready, as certain of a warm welcome as he has ever been.

AdorableCredit: Pet Haven Minnesota

A year ago, Greyson was a hand-fed orphan who fit in one palm and was not promised an easy road. Today he is a healthy, handsome, one-year-old cat with two personalities and a lifetime of headbutts saved up for whoever finally gets to keep him.

Turning one means something different for a kitten who started as small as Greyson did.

Happy Birthday Greyson! Credit: Jada Kitten Foster

Share this story with your friends. View more on Greyson and Pet Haven Minnesota on Instagram @pethavenmn and Facebook or pethavenmn.org. Follow along with his current foster, Jada, at @jadakittenfoster, and see where his journey began with Kris at @campwobblycat and Abby at @abbysfostercatchaos.

item.title: Two Kittens Thrown From a Moving Truck Soaked in Bleach Held On to Each Other Until Help Arrived
item.description:
Two young kittens named Dolly and Monroe were thrown from a moving car inside a duffel bag, and a few weeks later, the two of them have come back stronger, healthier, and refusing to be apart.

Dolly and MonroeCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

It began on Manchester Road in St. Louis, with a moment that would have been easy to miss. A woman driving by noticed a duffel bag flying out of the window of a moving pickup truck. Something about it felt wrong to her, and instead of continuing, she pulled over to look.

Inside the bag were two kittens, each only about five and a half months old, both soaked in what appeared to be bleach. She gathered them up and drove straight to the Humane Society of Missouri's headquarters on Macklind Avenue. The veterinary team met her at the door and got to work, washing the chemical from their fur and checking every inch for harm.

The kittens were thin, frightened, and worn down by whatever had led them into that bag. What they were not, for the first time, was alone.

Monroe, still damp from her first bath, the day she arrived at the shelterCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

One of the first photos taken of Monroe shows her still damp from that initial bath, her white coat clinging to a frame far too small, her eyes wide and unsure. The volunteers examined both kittens carefully for any damage to their skin, their eyes, and their ears.

Over the days that followed, the veterinarians kept the two girls close, watching for any lasting effects and running tests that would ensure the kittens were truly in the clear. The news, when it came, was good. "This is an incredibly disturbing act of cruelty, but it is also a powerful example of how one person's decision to stop and help can save a life," Kathy Warnick of the Humane Society of Missouri shared with LoveMeow.

Dolly, bright-eyed and curious, stopping to see what everyone is doingCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

Dolly recovered like a cat with somewhere to be. She is the one with the small black cap set high on her white head, the one who walks right up to see what you are doing and tips her chin for a better look.

A few short weeks made all the difference. The kitten who had arrived underweight and afraid grew rounder, brighter, and bolder, until the fear of that first day had nowhere left to sit.

Dolly settled in as though she has always lived hereCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

These days Dolly stretches out along the back of a chair as though she has always owned it, one paw folded neatly beneath her chest. She settles in wherever she pleases and dares anyone to suggest otherwise.

Wherever Dolly goes, Monroe is not far behind. The two of them are rarely found in separate corners of a room, and where one of them lands, the other tends to appear a moment later.

Monroe watching the roomCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

Monroe is the quieter study of the two, with a bold patch of black drawn over one eye and ear like a mask she was born wearing. She watches a room before she joins it, then folds herself down beside her companion and lets the world come to her.

None of it would have been possible without the stranger who trusted her own instincts on Manchester Road. "Because she acted, these two kittens are safe, receiving medical care and have the opportunity for the happy lives they deserve," Warnick shared.

Two of them rarely far apartCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

You can see what they mean to each other in the smallest moments. Dolly leans in to groom the top of Monroe's head, and Monroe closes her eyes and lets her, the two of them pressed close on a shared blanket as though the rest of the room has fallen away.

Both girls have since been spayed and cleared by the veterinary team, and they are now looking for a home together. Whoever takes one of these girls will certainly be taking both, because they've made it clear they come as a set.

Monroe today, healthy and settledCredit: Humane Society of Missouri

Not long ago, Dolly and Monroe were tossed from a moving car and left on the side of the road with nothing. Today they are healthy, inseparable, and entirely themselves, two kittens who decided their story was only getting started.

Share this story with your friends. More on Dolly and Monroe and the Humane Society of Missouri on Instagram @hsmopets and Facebook, or directly at hsmo.org.
